在2017年，中国的经济尽管在快速增长，但收入差距仍然是一个显著的问题。城市和农村之间、不同地区之间的收入水平差异明显，同时高收入群体和低收入群体间的财富不平等状况依然存在。对于很多城市居民来说，这种收入差距在日常生活中是显而易见的。
#### 答案：1（非常同意）

### 2. 为了社会公平，人们的物质生活水平差异应该很小。
#### 理由：
社会公平是许多人追求的目标，而生活水平差异过大会导致社会矛盾和不满。因此，适当地缩小物质生活水平的差异能够促进社会和谐。然而，完全消除差异既不切实际，也可能削弱个人奋斗的动力。
#### 答案：2（同意）

### 3. 缩小高收入者和低收入者之间的差距是政府的责任。
#### 理由：
政府在资源分配和制度设计上有关键作用，可以通过税收调整、福利政策等方法来缩小收入差距。政府的调控是实现社会公平的必要手段之一。因此，政府确实有责任在经济发展中努力缩小收入差距。
#### 答案：1（非常同意）

### 4. 我国的社会福利让人变得懒散。
#### 理由：
中国的社会福利体系相比于一些西方国家仍不够完善，福利整体水平较低，因此尚不足以让人产生依赖懒散的情况。社会福利主要是为了解决基本生活保障问题，帮助困难群体走出困境。
#### 答案：5（非常不同意）

我认为政府在调节收入差距和提供基本社会保障方面有着不可推卸的责任。政府应该通过税收、福利和公共服务等手段有效减少不平等，但同时要避免福利过多导致懒散。

   - 理由：作为生活在城市的农业户口居民，您的经济改善可能更多地依靠于政府政策的支持。因此，您可能倾向于认为政府有责任采取措施缩小收入差距。
   - 答案：1（非常同意）

4. **我国的社会福利让人变得懒散。**
   - 理由：由于您的职业经历和目前的经济状况，您可能无法获得许多社会福利。对您而言，社会福利的不足可能是困扰，而非让人懒散的因素。
   - 答案：5（非常不同意）

请注意，这些答案是基于假设背景的合理推测，实际情况可能会根据个人看法而有所不同。
Valid answers saved: ['1', '2', '1', '5']
正在生成第4062条记录...
agent思考过程： 理由：

1. 关于“我国的收入差距太大了”这一观点，对于务农人员来说，收入水平相对较低，与城市居民或其他行业的从业者相比，可能更能感受到收入差距的存在。因此，我可能会认为这个观点是合理的。

2. 对于“为了社会公平，人们的物质生活水平差异应该很小”这一观点，从一个农业户口的务农者的角度来看，可能更希望能缩小物质生活水平的差异，以获得更好的生活条件，从而倾向于支持这个观点。

3. 对于“缩小高收入者和低收入者之间的差距是政府的责任”这一观点，作为普通劳动者，我可能会认为政府在调节收入分配、提供公平机会方面有责任，因此更可能同意这一观点。

4. 关于“我国的社会福利让人变得懒散”，在农村地区，社会福利可能不是特别优渥，更多的人依靠自身劳动来维持生活，因此我可能不太赞同这个说法。

答案：

1. 我国的收入差距太大了。 - 1（非常同意）

2. 为了社会公平，人们的物质生活水平差异应该很小。 - 2（同意）

3. 缩小高收入者和低收入者之间的差距是政府的责任。 - 1（非常同意）

4. 我国的社会福利让人变得懒散。 - 5（非常不同意）

Tuesday, October 4, 2011

I was tickled to learn a new skill today! Well, one of those things I see and think "Oh, at some point, I want to learn to do that, but I don't know how." Yes, there are many things on that list...especially involving fabric...

So maybe it wasn't on my list until I saw this super adorable little pumpkin amigurumi in Ana Paula Rimoli's book Amigurumi World Seriously Cute Crochet!

I am working on an awesome lil' pumpkin doll from the book for Hudson. As I worked on the bottom, it needed to be "felted". So off to the local yarn shop and home with some wool yarn. I couldn't figure out what was wrong with this pumpkin base! Why was it so large? Oh...it needed to be felted...yes! How do I do that? Wool shrinks...okay...I can do this! Oh yes, I remember this from the knitting article I read....so in the hot water it goes, swish, scrub, cold water, hot water, swish, scrub...when nothing happened I turned to google:

At Knitty.com I learned the following essentials:

1. You agitate it while it is wet in order to felt it (swish and scrub)
2. It takes a while (stay and scrub some more)

Tuesday, September 27, 2011

I believe I have an insurmountable amount of stuffing.

The last few nights I have woken from wild dreams of building committee assignments, alternating proposals, committee members adding last minute requests, and similar organizational nightmares. These dreams were reminiscent of the infamous T Badge Tower dreams of old only now they contain a never-ending assortment of materials.

I imagine a committee meeting scheduled, and I am adding the last minute details to the proposal when a request comes in to add one more item which would require a completely new design. I was calm and a quick regret about artistic differences that arose between committee members, however at times various pet projects came to heart. None of them were real. A lifelike configuration manifested from three or four very real local works as a new fantasy landscape diagram, buildings transforming and overlapping through the course of the dream presentations. Committee meetings streamed through the night in agonizing detail.

I woke up, set my completed drawings aside, and ordered a cold bottle of water. Then I woke up. My stomached growled for a post-meeting snack or was it breakfast already? I lay there in the last few moments as I ruminated on the randomness and tried to focus on the last building--no, I caught it and saw it dissolve as I awoke again. I lay on my side and stared at the shadows around the room, reminding myself that there were no midnight trips to sketch and meet. Eventually, my conscious mind won and I was nearly awake.

I stood in the shower, letting the water massage my back, hoping to recover more fully when suddenly after the steam had engulfed the bathroom I remembered my grand idea with absolute certainty. Ah, yes... I needed more stuffing.

My closet is full of fabric and other craft supplies. And yes, there are multiple containers of stuffing, deserving of it's own shelf. I am sure it is breeding. A light goes out and they double. But this important idea to buy more stuffing - I'm going to blame on sleep deprivation. I really have no idea why I thought it important for the whole thing to come together when I've already started looking for additional storage for the bird fluff.

I think what happens is that when we get overwhelmed we may look internally for ways to "re-organize" or "make do" with what we have already. Maybe that's why I make such ridiculous connections in my dreams!   Or maybe, just maybe, I'm cursed with far too much "stuffing of fluff". DH would likely see things this way...Thus, today we have also donated an enormous pile to the Rescue Mission--and I may not have taken any "stuffing" out to the car yet.

Friday, February 11, 2011

I recently watched a strange movie called Re-walked: Path to Breathe
In this nearly five year old film, John Francis reflects on a time during which he refused to speak or travel by motorized vehicle. John began walking the day after his 27th birthday.

He would say nothing for 17 years. He maintained silence for 17 years.

How much does your life change when you choose not to complain? What sort of man explains an answer through a smile instead of telling you what a terrible thing the question was for that day?

I struggle with sharing news as it happens, which is why I didn't announce that I was 3 1/2 months pregnant with a boy until this week. Though I'm certainly not a silent individual, I find that my thoughts and words often need to be filtered....

Learning to remain silent is a feat not to be taken lightly. When comment after comment comes up regarding one's actions or significant life changes, it is difficult to remember that selecting the appropriate time, or not complaning to those who don't know the entire situation is better. The more you explain, the more often others will comment rather than respect. After all, it involves them when you give complaints a voice.

How does watching the production of an artist known for his silence for nearly two decades accomplish?   A reminder that silence has it's merits on occasion!

Thursday, January 20, 2011

(in reference to "Geeking Out with Art Quilts" Workshop at Crissy Field devised by the *InStiches team)
Since I will be moving shortly, I wanted to take on one set of challenges through 3 of the surface design work stations offered. I told myself: I would not worry too much about the perfection of their execution. I would work in "series" and let each piece teach me something from the workshop. 

1st: Angelina! This lovely fiber is really fun to just play with...think of the Easter grass you had as a child...now imagine you could press it so it lay down on itself...yep! You take a few wisps of the fiber, lay it on a piece of tracing paper and gently press with a medium high to high iron for 15-30 seconds. Note to self: If you print something on the paper, it transfers.

 Adding the Exploded silk: I was even given options in colors/hues... Although in my embellishment I will be adding additional threads... originally this was such a bright, beautiful, piece!

Fusible Applique: Why have I avoided this particular technique for all this time?!?!? Oh yes, I was a theater costumer and there is a stigma about quickly made and docked-the attatchment method to seamlessly (or rather, cheaply) alter garments. What I failed to consider was, well, there are better products than adding Sobo glue to an existing costume and putting trim on top of the additions. That particular method works for quite a lot of quick and dirty theater. Why do we fear efficiency at times? It's weird.

Such easy applique...and fun! Freezing, heating, using baking parchment, was a pleasant evening...especially adding 2 inch heels. : ~ )  If one's going to celebrate the elements of design in their life...celebrate every possibility...

Combine two and begin the maps...Ah, surprise! A large planet/eye ended up in the center of my planned small bits looking like a junk yard of parts...I will definitely have to work with some shading on this one.
Thankfully, through the day the QR Station Calm was open for business. Pep rally, with a huge and friendly group.

What an adventure to come!

Thursday, July 1, 2010

As my mind ponders art, over and over the call of Gothic Saints urges riveting (soul as popcorn!?! what possessed eons? perhaps too many a needles for ol' callused hands...random note: I suspect...There is some joke about witchery typing with Charcoal colored hands...but that's a tale for another day).

Today's Featured artist is Gustav Klimt an Austrian painter (1862-1918) whose symbolism and use of organic forms grips the soul with playful and serious wonder. Known for his work with the art nouveau movement, Gustav blended nature among surreal human embraces - fashioning their elements through decorative motifs and hauntingly beautiful symbolism. Truly, he was one of the first to break free from the strict dictates of realism to celebrate the swell and fall of the mind in artistic chaos.   His figures seduce in their touch.


The Expectation (1905-1909)
You can feel the anticipation aching. His work often incorporated the symbolism with the natural equivalent of universal forces. Man becomes singular in detail and many in the image's movement. Yet the forms speak to individual stories and require thought to understand their connections. There is a promise of something behind what is seen- it may be more clear in "Adele"


Lady with Hat and Feather Boa (1909)

Hope II (1907-8)
Gustave Klimt did not shy away from conveying inner life and how the most vulnerable moments impact our beauty, and understanding of what connects the body to the soul. To hypnotize...to wonder is art's great gift. For more on Klimt's life and works you may enjoy the touching synastry explored in "The Painted Kiss"- a semi fictional novel by Elizabeth Hickey.

Monday, May 25, 2009

Today's post derives inspiration from the Sojourner Truth. Sojourner was born a slave in the the late 18th century. After a deeply religious experience Sojourner vowed to travel across the country in the pursuit of abolition. She was early civil rights advocate and mesmerizing speaker. Her true testament can be found in Ain't I A Woman.

Lately I've been reading "Seize the Lightning" by Jean Marie Wilson. On a brief romantic interlude
I was struck by the thematic nature of a life's posted testimony. The gleaming colors of shared art, inspired through passage...echo of truth's soul searching revelations driving passion and desire forward- reclaiming innate wonder through visual representations....

Perhaps William Tell would have preserved breath's absence practical through the embroidered lens of seconds lost to Shakespeare or Poe's gallows humor? : ~ ) The world is fortunate Sojouner Truth chose words to share her enlightenment with the world.

Yesterday this summer's Cricut Expression was my newest toy!

The starter pack provided a simplistic fantasy world where fawns frolicked merrily in bold array among life-like posies, trees. Yes. Wheels of the gentle season turning...though fare less the dime and rhyme...





A "must-have"? Perhaps not, but for serious at home crafters it is a delightful tool. The cricut does require a large workstation in comparison to other cutter brands such as the Slice and has a few more installments required than quaint rechargeable models (not to mention cartridges and keyboard covers). However, Cricut's amazing selection of card design cartridges, customizeable SVGs (one can create logos great detail in Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop if you know how), and high vector precision cutouts make this model versatile enough to meet the needs and doodles of before man's song danced through echo and unspoken lyrics...along time's cover of passing page but a measure.







Do you have a Cricut? Which one??? How do you rate compare- to my winding walk among lilies with their unfolding leaves faced to meet recaptured dreams adorning my garden's quick-lost

Today's inspirational featured artist... the famed engraver and master craftsman who forever changed the perspective of history. 
William Hogarth: 1697 - 1764
Through pen and precision, William Hogarth's illustrations capture a satirical narrative through the slow fall of London's privileged society. "A Rakes' Progress" highlights a man of wealthy family rise (or fall!) to corrupted politician within eight intensely depicted illustrations. Ah, perhaps Dickens might've remembered curiosity shop faces captured still in line's stirring prose!?!?

agent思考过程： 当然，这里是对每个观点进行的思考和选择：

1. **我国的收入差距太大了。**

   - **理由**：2017年的中国，收入差距问题一直是广受讨论的话题。作为一名来自农村的年轻人，可能在看到大城市中高收入人群的生活水平后，对收入差距有更明确的感知。这种差距在城乡之间尤为明显，因此很可能会觉得收入差距确实过大。

   - **答案**：1（非常同意）

2. **为了社会公平，人们的物质生活水平差异应该很小。**

   - **理由**：从农村背景来看，可能会更倾向于支持平等主义，认为过大的物质生活水平差异不利于社会的和谐和稳定。缩小差距可以提升整个社会的幸福感，所以可能会同意这种观点。

   - **答案**：2（同意）
